summary: Training data for the last 4 weeks shows only a single open-water swim session (5.2km, 153 min on Oct 3), with virtually no wellness data recorded — this makes it very difficult to assess fatigue, recovery, or training load trends. The absence of cycling and running sessions in the log is a significant concern given that the Marathon is just 99 days away and requires a consistent, progressive run build starting now. With the 10K race on November 8 as the nearest event in the plan, the priority this week should be controlled aerobic sharpening rather than heavy load.
suggestions: With the Marathon 99 days away, begin logging all three disciplines consistently every week — missing data prevents accurate load monitoring and makes it impossible to detect overtraining or under-recovery.

The November 8 10K race is your nearest event: ensure the Wk20 long ride on Nov 7 (the day before) is kept easy and genuinely aerobic — do not add Z3 Tempo blocks that day regardless of whether it is a bike-peak week.

Reconnect your Garmin sleep tracking — sleep score and body battery data are completely absent for the entire 4-week window, removing a key early-warning signal for accumulated fatigue heading into race week.

Your open-water swim pace of ~29:26/km (~2:57/100m) is slower than the ≤2:30/100m pool target in the plan; prioritise technique drills and consistent pool sessions to close this gap before the Ironman build begins.

For the Marathon target (sub-4h, ~5:45/km), ensure the Wk21 and Wk22 long runs (20km and 20.6km) are executed at the prescribed 6:15–6:45/km — these are the most important aerobic stimulus sessions in the current 4-week window.
